question: Who inaugurated the National Conference on ‘Environment – 2025’ in New Delhi on 29 March 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Droupadi Murmu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Droupadi Murmu**, the President of India, inaugurated the National Conference on ‘Environment – 2025’ in New Delhi on **29 March 2025**.
 
• The conference aimed to address critical environmental challenges and outline strategies for sustainable development in India by **2025**.
 
• As the head of state, Droupadi Murmu has been actively involved in promoting environmental sustainability and climate change awareness.
 
• The event brought together policymakers, environmentalists, scientists, and industry experts to discuss issues such as **climate change mitigation, renewable energy adoption, and biodiversity conservation**.
 
• The conference is considered a significant step towards fulfilling India’s commitment to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**:

 
 
• A set of 17 global goals adopted by UN member nations in 2015 to address pressing global challenges by 2030.
 
• Key goals include eradicating poverty, ensuring clean water and sanitation, promoting renewable energy, and combating climate change.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity Conservation**:
 
 
• Refers to the protection and management of biodiversity to ensure its sustainability for future generations.
 
• India is a signatory to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) and has implemented initiatives like the National Biodiversity Action Plan.
 
 
 
• **Climate Change Mitigation**:
 
 
• Involves reducing greenhouse gas emissions to minimize global warming and its effects.
 
• India has committed to achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2070 as part of its COP26 pledge.
 
 
 
• **Renewable Energy in India**:
 
 
• India is among the top countries in the world for renewable energy installation, with a focus on solar, wind, and hydroelectric power.
 
• The government has set a target of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel energy capacity by 2030.
